direct_answer:
At year-end 2024, Aker BP’s employee workforce (2,962 employees) comprised 2,231 men and 731 women (i.e., 24.7% women) [Source 2][Source 3]. Employment type disclosures provided indicate 51 temporary employees and 36 part-time employees [Source 2], and the company states it does not hire employees on zero-hour contracts [Source 8].

Women held 31% of Executive Management Team (EMT) positions at year-end (EMT: 16 members; women: 31%) [Source 4].
compliance_rationale: The report provides a gender breakdown of employees (men/women) and some employment-type information (temporary and part-time counts; statement of no zero-hour contracts) [Source 2][Source 8]. It also provides the percentage of women in the Executive Management Team (31%), enabling the percentage of women in that top management body to be stated [Source 4]. However, the ESRS S1-6 employment-type breakdown is incomplete versus ESRS categories (permanent/temporary/non-guaranteed hours) and lacks required methodological explanations (e.g., headcount vs FTE; point-in-time vs average; and financial statement cross-reference) in the retrieved passages.
disclosure_gaps: Breakdown of employees by ESRS employment type categories (permanent, temporary, non-guaranteed hours) by gender; only temporary and part-time counts are provided, and non-guaranteed hours are only addressed qualitatively (no zero-hour contracts) [Source 2][Source 8].

Methodological explanations required by ESRS S1-6 (headcount vs FTE; point-in-time vs average; assumptions/context; and cross-reference to the most representative number in the financial statements) are not provided in the retrieved passages.

Gender distribution at top management level in both number and percentage (ESRS S1-9): only a percentage for EMT is provided; the number of women in EMT is not explicitly stated (though total EMT members are given) [Source 4].

Management positions held by women beyond EMT (e.g., senior managers/managers) are not disclosed as a percentage; only workforce category counts by gender are partially provided for some categories (e.g., managers and senior professionals) [Source 2].
key_findings: Employees at year-end 2024: 2,962 total; 2,231 men and 731 women (24.7% women) [Source 2][Source 3].
Employment type indicators: 51 temporary employees and 36 part-time employees; no zero-hour contracts [Source 2][Source 8].
Top management (EMT) gender representation: women are 31% of EMT at year-end (16 members total) [Source 4].
